result.summary: Adds wallet and RPC support for sending transactions to BIP 352 Silent Payment addresses. It introduces a PaymentDestination abstraction to accommodate destinations whose output scripts depend on the spending inputs, updates coin selection to ensure at least one eligible private key is available to derive shared secrets, and adds dynamic derivation of taproot outputs during transaction creation. It also records Silent Payment recipients in the wallet database and records placeholder metadata to safeguard fee-bumping compatibility across wallet software versions.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core users cannot send bitcoin to BIP 352 Silent Payment addresses. This blocks users from transacting with recipients relying on Silent Payments for address reuse prevention and receiver privacy without relying on third-party wallets.
evidence: PR description: "This PR is part of integrating silent payments into Bitcoin Core. It is the second iteration of https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/28201. Status and tracking for the project is managed in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/28536"
PR description: "any operation that produces a silent payments tx that is not safe to fee bump later is blocked; this includes operations that create psbts and send with add_to_wallet=False"
result.scope_notes: Touches wallet internals across coin selection, transaction building, wallet persistence, fee bumping, and RPC parsing. It adds a new diagnostic RPC `scantxforsilentpayments` and uses a backward compatibility mechanism in CWalletTx serialization where a transaction is marked as replaced by its own txid to prevent older node versions from invalidating silent payments outputs via RBF.
result.changed_since_previous: The fundamental design remains unchanged; commits and tests have been maintained across rebases over prerequisite updates in BIP 352 support.
result.card: Adds wallet and RPC support for sending to BIP 352 Silent Payment addresses. Currently, Bitcoin Core wallet users cannot pay Silent Payment recipients, restricting adoption of receiver privacy features. The implementation adapts coin selection to require derivation-eligible inputs, generates recipient taproot outputs dynamically, persists Silent Payment metadata for fee-bumping, and adds the scantxforsilentpayments RPC. This PR is part of the project tracked in issue #28536 and depends on BIP 352 base PR #35301.

risk.why: A flaw in the shared secret derivation or taproot output generation during transaction creation could produce unspendable outputs and permanently burn user funds.
